Cyber Attack Disrupts Transportation & Logistics Firms Across Poland

A major cyber attack targeting the Transportation & Logistics industry is causing widespread disruption to firms across Poland, with several companies reporting system outages and halted operations. The attack, believed to involve ransomware, began in the early hours of Wednesday and remains active, according to industry sources.

Affected firms include Wistal Transport, PolCargo Logistics, and Mazovia Freight Solutions, all of which have confirmed that their IT systems have been compromised. As a result, scheduling, route planning, and cargo tracking services have been suspended or severely limited. Workers at several distribution centers in Gdańsk, Łódź, and Katowice have been sent home, while others remain on standby as companies struggle to restore access to critical systems.

"The scale of this attack is unprecedented for our sector," said Tomasz Janicki, spokesperson for the Polish Association of Transport Operators. "Firms are working around the clock to contain the impact, but the situation remains very serious."

Industry analysts estimate that at least 40% of Poland's mid-sized Transportation & Logistics firms are currently affected, with hundreds of lorries and delivery vehicles unable to receive updated instructions. Employee unions have raised concerns about job security and pay as the disruption stretches into a second day.

"Workers are frustrated and anxious," said Agnieszka Pluta, regional union representative. "We urge companies to prioritize communication and support for their staff during this difficult time."

Polish authorities have launched an investigation and are working with affected firms to assess the full extent of the breach. As the attack continues, industry stakeholders warn that recovery could take days or longer, with significant operational and financial consequences for Transportation & Logistics firms nationwide.
